title: Task starter preparation assumes a single Schedule despite existing Program authoring support

locators: tests/contracts/test_program_task_starters.py::program_source: existing two-stage copy then SiLU Program with the original registered SiLU Workload
5bb474c6:src/open_cake_ir/lab/python_reference.py::read_skeleton delegates every Python starter to the single-Schedule parser
evidence.scope: Task preparation and executable handoff defect. The Compiler already owns Program semantics; no new IR or GPU capability is inferred.

observation: A Python Program candidate can use the existing Program frontend, authoring environment and builder, but the same complete source cannot serve as an ordinary task starter. Task preparation reads a root lowering field that Program does not declare, and baseline admission only examines one kernel source.
proposed_change: Select the existing Program parser from an explicit static cake.program declaration. Bind every stage to the original Workload; validate complete public ABI and common backend. Lower with Compiler.lower_program and validate all sealed stage sources and launch records through program_components. Preserve the single-Schedule path. Native comparison of Program starters remains a named refusal.
promotion_disposition: Promoted to existing Task/Lab preparation and baseline admission. The authoring route entry_point remains only a default single-Schedule entry; it is not a Program device function. No added IR field or second Run engine. Runtime Program timing qualification is owned separately.

verified_by.tests: 66 passed, 0 skipped, 0 failed: program_task_starters, python_task_reference, python_paired_studies, metal_preflight and task_launch
verified_by.scope: Real static Program parsing, Workload binding, TaskLab preflight, task package, source build and sealed multi-stage baseline contracts with explicit CPU Executor/provider/compiler doubles. Later-stage source/grid substitution, missing/reordered stages and mixed backend/target are refused. No provider call, native device compile, GPU correctness or timing qualification.
